checks.evidence: RawData directory names give 488 recordings and 26 base tasks. source_coverage.json (sha256 1dc0199e...) gives 787 parsing files over 19 tasks, 9 empty (AB01 stairs_1_2/4/6/8/10_down; AB05 and AB10 normal_walk_1_2-0/2-5, matching README 108/139; the AB01 ones are unexplained). That is 403 recordings with any parsing file, 398 with non-empty ones. The 7 unsegmented tasks are meander, obstacle_walk, poses, push, start_stop, tug_of_war and twister, as README 278 lists. Event classes from README 272-277: heel strike for dynamic_walk, incline_walk, normal_walk (skip by README 273), stairs, walk_backward and weighted_walk (6); plate pass for cutting and tire_run (2); trunk-velocity lift_weight plus pelvis-velocity ball_toss, curb_down, curb_up, jump, lunges, side_shuffle, sit_to_stand, squats, step_ups and turn_and_step (11). The jump_hop 20 N contact exception (README 274) is noted in the audit. GroupTasks.m (Code.zip), mapped expression by expression: normal 2-0/2-5 -> run, skip -> calisthenics, heel/toe walk -> misc, hop -> jump_in_place, side_shuffle -> jump_across, obstacle_walk -> step_over. README 272 lists 'shuffling' among the heel-strike tasks. Reading it as normal_walk_1_shuffle (0.4 m/s, GroupTasks 'walk') is consistent with side_shuffle's identical left/right typed windows (150/150), but the audit does not state the ambiguity.

checks.name: Converter findings F1-F6 against code
checks.evidence: F1: convert_gtech_phase_to_parquet.m 443-490 keeps the leg with more intervals (tie: earlier first start) and drops the other. My own re-implementation on the inventory (conditions expanded as expand_parsing_conditions 1573-1597 does) gives kept 8171 and dropped 4948, with identical per-activity counts. The 498 = normal_walk 349 (only the 14 running files 2-0/2-5 carry both legs) + stairs 149. Not counted in the 498: jump_hop drops 127 per-contact intervals (README 274 contact events), probably near-duplicate both-leg windows (10 of 12 hop files equal L/R). F2: window_from_parsing (time converter 319-357) takes [min start, max end] over every Nx2 field, and reference leg = earlier first start. Note: 85 recordings have no parsing file and 5 more have only empty ones, so 90 recordings carry no source intervals (F2 says 85). F3: the fallback (phase 217-226) fires only when both legs are empty after condition expansion, and only for names containing sit_to_stand or jump. utilities/segment_sit_stand_transitions.m and segment_jump_cycles.m default to 600/400 N and 25 deg/s. Every sit_to_stand/jump file in the inventory has fields, so 'should never fire' holds. F4: parse_gtech_activity_matlab.m 22-39 labels every normal_walk level_walking (2-0/2-5 parsed as speed 2.0/2.5; skip as a variant); GroupTasks says run and calisthenics. F5: stairs height_m 0.15 and step_number = pass index (96-105); curb_up/curb_down 0.15 and step_ups 0.20 (240-251); the paper XML Table 1 gives 152 for the stair columns; no curb or step-up height is found in the paper text. F6: the time converter writes LForceX/ForceZ to grf_anterior/grf_lateral (501-506); the phase converter maps ForceX/ForceZ the same way (794-835).

checks.name: CoP frame mismatch
checks.evidence: The time converter's cop_local (573-636) transforms global CoP by R^T (cop - Tr) into the calcn body frame and writes local x/z/y as cop_anterior/lateral/vertical. docs/reference/index.md (row 'Centre of pressure') defines CoP as a 'Ground-frame point x, y, ±z' with only the origin dataset-specific. A foot-fixed frame rotates with the foot, so this is an axis (frame) mismatch, not just an origin difference.

checks.name: Decision D-GT23-C01-1
checks.evidence: Mechanics pass: decision.json equals handoff decisions[0]; appended to a copy of backlog.json it passes validate_backlog (open would be D-GT23-C04-1 and this; the queue_note naming D-HIST-04-1/2 is stale, since only D-GT23-C04-1 is open now). The order is neutral (most to none), stated in options_order and the builder (line 709). The recommendation appears only in the fold, the reply hint is neutral, and the options table has 'Left out' first plus defer. The check (backward-walking arrows opposite) is visible in the made-up figure. It is José's call: docs/reference defines +x as 'the walking direction' while the frame is drawn 'facing right', which does not determine non-forward tasks, and any answer sets a cross-dataset convention. Completeness: (a) C 'lab only' and defer have the same outcome (no GT23 forward/sideways values, lab values kept); C only makes it final. (b) The literal reading of the existing rule, +x = direction of travel where travel is steady (which would give values for walk_backward and side_shuffle, with braking/propulsion signs flipping relative to facing), is not offered, so José cannot choose the rule as written. (c) Minor: B's consequence lists 'forward walking, running, stairs, curbs and step-ups' but its forward class also holds start_stop and tire_run, and meander (forward overground walking with a turning heading) is excluded as 'heading_changes' without saying so.
